name: Hawaii
one: Hawaii mails a ballot to every registered voter. Below: how to send it back and the deadlines.
sec:
Vote by mail or absentee

Can’t get to your polling place on Election Day? Here is how to vote by mail in Hawaii, from the state’s own election office and its laws. Checked October 21, 2026.

Getting your ballot

Tuesday, October 27Passed

To have your ballot mailed to a different address, your application must reach your County Elections Division by Tuesday, October 27, 2026 (7 days before Election Day). (official page)

Send it back by

Tuesday, November 3Passed

Your ballot must be received by your County Elections Division by 7 p.m. on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026. Mailing it on time is not enough; it must arrive by then. (official page)

That date has passed. You can still vote in person, early or on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3.You can still vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3. When and where to vote early.

Hawaii’s own page on voting by mail

At school away from home, in Hawaii or in another state? What Hawaii says about students is under Show more.

Who can vote by mail

Hawaii votes by mail. Every registered voter is mailed a ballot automatically, at the address on their voter registration; there is nothing to ask for. Voters who will be away from home can ask for the ballot to go to another address. (official page)

How to ask for a ballot

  • Automatically. You do not need to ask. Ballots for the November 3, 2026 general election are mailed so that voters have them by Friday, October 16, 2026. If yours has not come, call your County Elections Division. Open it (official page)
  • By mail. If you will be away from your Hawaii home, fill in the Absentee Ballot Application to have your ballot mailed to a temporary address (it is good only for the election year you send it in). It asks for your Hawaii driver's license or state ID number, or the last four digits of your Social Security number, and your signature; if you cannot sign, mark the line and have a witness sign. Send it to your County Elections Division (the addresses are on the form). Open it (official page)
  • In person. You can also vote in person, or register and vote the same day, at a voter service center in your county. Open it (official page)

How to send it back

  • By mail. Mail it in the prepaid return envelope (no stamp needed). Leave time for it to arrive by 7 p.m. on Election Day. (official page)
  • Drop box. Drop it at a place of deposit (ballot drop box) in your county. (official page)
  • In person. Voter service centers are open for in-person voting; see the state's list of voter service centers and drop boxes. (official page)

What the envelope needs

Sign the return envelope. Your ballot cannot be counted without that signature, and it is checked against the signature on your voter registration. (official page)

Track your ballot

Track your ballot on Hawaii’s own site (official page)

Vote early in person instead

Tuesday, October 20, 2026 to Tuesday, November 3, 2026.

Voter service centers are open from Tuesday, October 20, through Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, 2026 (closed Sundays), for in-person voting, accessible voting and same-day registration. (official page)

Students

At school in Hawaii, away from home

The state says a Hawaii resident at a college in Hawaii may send in the Absentee Ballot Application to have their ballot mailed to their campus address, and must send a new one each election year they are away from their Hawaii home. (official page)

At school in another state, with Hawaii as home

The state says a Hawaii resident at college out of state who wants to vote in Hawaii elections must send in the Absentee Ballot Application to have their ballot mailed to their current mailing address, and must send a new one each election year they are away. (official page)

Military and overseas

Military voters, their families and U.S. citizens overseas register and ask for a ballot with the Federal Post Card Application (FPCA); send a new request each election year. New registrants must get it to their County Elections Division by October 26, 2026; voters already registered must ask by October 27, 2026. You can ask to get your ballot by mail, email or fax. It must be received by 7 p.m. on Election Day. If your ballot does not come, use the Federal Write-In Absentee Ballot. (official page)

Hawaii in the Federal Voting Assistance Program’s guide

Good to know

  • Hawaii law (HRS 11-13) says you do not gain or lose a residence just by being away as a student, that a person can have only one residence for voting, and that voting in another state's election, by absentee ballot or in person, ends your Hawaii residence.
  • If you have moved or changed your mailing address or name, update your voter registration so your ballot reaches you.
  • Paper voter registration forms for the general election must reach your County Elections Division by October 26, 2026; you can also register online, or in person at a voter service center through Election Day.
  • Voters with a disability who cannot read standard print can ask on the application for a ballot sent by email.
Where this comes from: 6 pages of Hawaii’s election office, its laws and the federal guide
